slice: Triumph TF suspension/setups/chassis depth + 2027 model-year changes for KTM, Husqvarna, GasGas and Triumph

records.statement: A long-time tester's motocross baseline for the TF 250-X keeps the stock 4.7 N/mm fork springs and 56 N/mm shock spring, with the fork 3 mm up, fork compression and rebound 8 clicks out, 103 mm race sag, shock high-speed compression 1 turn out, low-speed 7 out and rebound 10 out. It aims for a bit more hold-up at both ends than stock while keeping comfort.

source.name: Keefer Inc Tested: 2026 250 MX Baseline Suspension Settings

records.notes: Identical settings were published in the 2025 edition (Feb 2025) and repeated for 2026 (Jun 2026). Tester weight not stated. Source describes the 250-X as well balanced out of the box and needing less tuning than its class rivals. Clicker counts are from full stiff.

records.statement: A tester's 2026 450 baseline for the TF 450-X runs a 4.8 N/mm fork spring with the fork flush to 2 mm up, compression 8-9 out and rebound 11 out; the shock keeps the 58 N/mm spring with low-speed compression 9 out, high-speed 1.5 turns out and rebound 11 out. The bike is described as soft and comfortable but needing stiffening to feel balanced off the throttle.

source.name: Keefer Inc Tested: 2026 450 MX Baseline Suspension Settings

records.notes: Sag not listed for the Triumph in this table. 4.8 N/mm differs from the 5.0 N/mm stock rate reported for the RC (see conflicts): it may be the tester's choice rather than the stock rate. Same article suggests aftermarket clamps to improve off-throttle front-end feel. Southern California tracks.

records.statement: Testers repeatedly point to aftermarket triple clamps as the main chassis fix for the TF's front end: the 450-X is called soft and hard to feel off the throttle, and stiffer or split clamps are suggested; one tester also found the front harder to lean into corners than he wanted, while praising straight-line predictability.

values.stock_clamp_torque: 25 N·m bottom / 30 N·m top (OEM figure quoted by tester)

source.name: Keefer Inc Tested: 2026 450 MX Baseline Suspension Settings

records.notes: Combined from the 2026 450 baseline article and a March 2025 clamp test on the TF 250-X/TF 450-RC (same author). The clamp test kept standard offset and reported no fork slip at normal torque. The same tester noted more vibration than most Japanese 450s except the KX450.

records.statement: Aftermarket one-piece clamps for the TF 250-X (2024-2026) and TF 250-E (2025-2026) are sold in a fixed 22 mm offset, presented as a balance of high-speed stability and quick corner entry; Triumph does not publish the stock clamp offset.

source.name: Motostorm: XTRIG ROCS Tech fixed offset 22mm steering plates Triumph TF 250-X

records.notes: Stock offset not found in any Triumph spec sheet or magazine technical overview searched; a tester running a standard-offset aftermarket clamp did not change offset. Product description from a European retailer.

records.statement: For 2027 the TF 250-X gets updated Neken triple clamps forged and machined from 7075-T6 aluminium, aimed at better front-end feel and tracking, plus new tool-free suspension adjusters; frame, swingarm and wheels are carried over.

source.name: Triumph press release via Motor Sports NewsWire: 2027 race-proven refinements for TF 250-X

records.notes: Offset not stated. Carry-over of frame/swingarm/wheels from autoevolution (2026-09).

records.statement: Triumph revised the 2027 TF 250-X KYB fork and shock settings for balance, damping control and feedback to match the updated engine and clutch, but publishes no clicker or spring values; hardware (48 mm AOS coil fork, 310 mm; piggyback shock, 305 mm) is unchanged.

source.name: Triumph press release via Motor Sports NewsWire: 2027 race-proven refinements for TF 250-X

records.notes: No numbers published; check the 2027 owner's handbook for stock clickers.

records.statement: Triumph's 2026 TF 250-X KYB update targeted mid-stroke control to improve chassis balance and cornering stability; no clicker or valving detail was given.

source.name: Enduro21: First look 2026 Triumph TF 250-X

records.notes: Quoted from Triumph statement in launch coverage. Direction/amount of valving change not published.

records.statement: On a deep, watered sand track an 80 kg tester found the stock 450-RC rear sat high and twitchy on sandy downhills; backing rear preload off a couple of turns to about 40 mm static sag and 102 mm race sag fixed it, with stock clickers. He warned that mid-30s static sag is not enough for this chassis.

source.name: ADB Magazine: MX Aussie launch Triumph TF 450-RC

records.notes: Smooth sand track with no chatter, so clickers were not tested. Media launch (Ride Park, Victoria, Australia).

records.topic: 250-X spring choice for a 90 kg rider
records.statement: A 90 kg tester found the stock springs (built for 70-80 kg) too soft, the medium (80-90 kg) set still a little soft, and the hard (90 kg+) springs let him push properly, with no clicker changes needed.

source.name: MotoOnline: Tested 2024 Triumph TF 250-X

records.notes: Soft loamy, well-watered private track (Australia). Spring rates for medium/hard sets not given in N/mm.

records.statement: Testers running 100-102 mm race sag found the stock fork soft: faster riders added 2-3 compression clicks, heavier (190 lb+) vet riders left built-up air in the fork as a temporary stiffener, and lighter riders softened the fork to match the shock. Lowering the fork 3 mm in the clamps calmed a busy front in fast rough corners at some cost to mid-corner precision.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: 2024 Triumph TF 250-X

records.notes: Southern California tracks incl. Perris. Also fitted a 49T rear sprocket (stock 48). 'Leaving air in' means not bleeding the fork caps; it is a temporary fix, not a spring substitute.

records.statement: Compared with the KTM's steel frame and WP air fork, the TF 250-X's aluminium chassis feels livelier and breaks traction a bit more, the spring fork puts more weight on the front, and the bike reacts more to fork height, sag and shock high-speed compression changes. Stock settings suit novice/intermediate riders around 165 lb, and testers ended up near stock clickers.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 Triumph TF250-X

records.notes: Paraphrased tester comparison; described as a difference in feel, not a flaw. Also recommends 49T (pro/intermediate) or 50T (novice) rear sprocket and says the 1.85 rear rim can be replaced by 2.15 with a 110 tyre.

records.statement: In a six-bike 250 shootout, testers rated the TF 250-X, with the Honda, as the most flexible (forgiving) chassis in corners, with exceptional handling and corner stability; they found it light and agile.

source.name: MX1 Onboard: We test the best six 250 bikes of 2025

records.notes: Spanish shootout (La Farm, Lleida). Frame stiffness not measured; subjective. Same test criticised gearbox effort and quickshift irregularities.

records.topic: 450 owner fork oil and spring change
records.statement: One 180 lb vet-expert owner reports stock 450 fork springs of 0.51 kg/mm (about 5.0 N/mm) and 310 cc of outer-chamber oil; he tried 0.48 kg/mm springs with 350 cc outer oil, fork 2 mm up and compression 15 out (stock 13), rebound 10 out, then planned to return to 0.51 kg/mm with a revalve.

source.name: Vital MX forum: Some Chassis and suspension work on the Triumph TF450

records.notes: Single owner report (May 2026). He used 0W-16 motor oil in the outers, which is not a recommendation. Stock compression of 13 out conflicts with 14 out in a magazine technical article (see conflicts).

records.statement: The same 180 lb owner, riding sand, loam and hardpack tracks, ran 105 mm race sag (axle about 5 mm back, about 103-104 mm with a centred axle), shock low-speed compression 16 out, high-speed 1 turn out and rebound 12 out on stock valving.

source.name: Vital MX forum: Some Chassis and suspension work on the Triumph TF450

records.notes: New York tracks (Compound MX, Broome Tioga, Jacksons MX). Shock spring rate not stated.

records.statement: One owner fitted aftermarket steering-head race cups, which changed the head angle and cut high-speed chatter on fast straights without hurting cornering (settings had to be retuned), and aftermarket head stays, which improved comfort on square-edged bumps with slightly less vibration above idle but more at idle; titanium pivot and engine-mount bolts showed no clear benefit.

source.name: Vital MX forum: Some Chassis and suspension work on the Triumph TF450

records.notes: Single owner, stock valving, partly cut-short test. The front still was not as planted as a Honda in his view.

records.statement: The 2026 TF 450-X differs from the 450-RC Edition in head stays, tyres, handlebar, seat cover and clutch cover, plus the new Exedy clutch hub, Belleville spring and selector star; rake 27.4 deg, trail 4.6 in and wheelbase 58.7 in are shared.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2026 Triumph TF 450-X Technical Overview

records.notes: Magazine technical overview based on Triumph info. Triumph's own media kit calls the mount change 'revised engine mounts' (tf-005).

records.statement: The TF 250-E uses the same Neken triple clamps as the TF 250-X, while the TF 450-E has its own clamps; both E models get softer springs and enduro damping, a 10 mm shorter fork (300 mm travel) and a 10 mm longer swingarm with an 18-inch rear wheel.

source.name: 1000PS: Triumph TF 250-E and TF 450-E Review 2025

records.notes: Press launch review (May 2025, bikes sold as 2026 in US). A second launch test (MOTORRAD) found the 250-E base setting firm but not harsh and said most riders can skip a suspension shop.

records.statement: Triumph's 2027 TF 250-X adds new valve guides for durability, a new clutch bearing and clutch pack with updated plates for the Exedy Belleville clutch, a new selector drum and detent wheel, revised mapping, revised KYB settings, tool-free adjusters, 7075-T6 Neken clamps, a revised chain guide, new switchgear with a separate stop/start switch, and all-black bodywork with new fork guards. Claimed 48 PS at 13,500 rpm and 104 kg wet are unchanged.

source.name: Triumph press release via Motor Sports NewsWire: 2027 race-proven refinements for TF 250-X

records.notes: Builds on tf-008 and tg-020; this is the full Triumph press text. Released after the 2026 MX2 title.

records.statement: The 2027 TF 250-X is cheaper than the 2026 bike: US $9,195 (2026: $9,795) and UK from GBP 8,395 (2026: from GBP 9,395).

source.name: Gear Patrol: 2027 Triumph TF 250-X updates

records.notes: US 2027 price from Gear Patrol and autoevolution; UK 2027 from Triumph release; 2026 prices from Dirt Rider (US) and Enduro21 (UK).

records.topic: 2027 status of TF 450 and C/E models
records.statement: As of October 2026 Triumph had announced 2027 changes only for the TF 250-X; the TF 450-X, TF 450-RC Edition, TF 250-C, TF 450-C, TF 250-E and TF 450-E were still being sold as 2025/2026 model-year bikes with no 2027 update published.

source.name: autoevolution: Triumph updates the TF 250-X motocrosser

records.notes: Absence of announcement, not a confirmed carry-over. The TF 450 cylinder-head recall (tg-001) applies to 2025-2026 450s. Recheck when Triumph announces the 450 range.

records.statement: KTM calls the 2027 250, 350 and 450 SX-F largely unchanged: new in-mould graphics with a touch of red, and engine updates for rideability and the latest FIM/AMA sound rules. Claimed wet weights are 234 lb (250), 236 lb (350) and 238 lb (450); WP XACT AER 48 mm fork (310 mm) and XACT shock (300 mm) carry over.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling: 2027 KTM SX-F Lineup First Look

records.notes: Manufacturer claims via magazine first look. This source prints the 450 bore as 94 mm; KTM and Husqvarna list 95 mm (see conflicts). See k45-010 for 450 detail (re-routed harness, frame wording).

records.statement: All 2027 KTM SX two-strokes are fuel-injected and get the new orange/red in-mould graphics. KTM's 2027 250 SX page lists frame updates (rear shock mount area and front frame wall thickness), updated engine mounts, a revised threaded radiator cap and new wiring-harness fixing points, with 99.4 kg claimed without fuel.

source.name: KTM: 2027 KTM 250 SX model page

records.notes: The frame/engine-mount wording matches KTM's description of earlier frame updates, so some items may be carried-over copy rather than 2027-new. The 1-year Premium Manufacturer's Warranty applies from MY2027. 300 SX also continues.

records.statement: The 2027 KTM 85 SX (17/14 and 19/16) is part of the refreshed SX range but no model-specific changes beyond new graphics were published.

source.name: ADB Magazine: KTM unveils 2027 SX motocross range

records.notes: Range-level press coverage only (ADB, RideApart).

records.statement: KTM's 2027 cross-country range is mostly unchanged: new red tank shrouds with in-mould graphics on the same chromoly frames, six-speed gearboxes and WP XACT closed-cartridge spring forks. The 350 XC-F and 125 XC return to the line-up, and the XC-F models work with the optional Connectivity Unit Offroad.

source.name: Enduro21: Quick Look 2027 KTM XC and XC-F range

records.notes: Australian release notes 125 XC and 450 XC-F as Australia-only there; US line-up per market may differ.

records.statement: KTM's 2027 US enduro bikes (150, 250 and 300 XC-W and 450 XCF-W) get a graphics update and unspecified 'refined engine packages'; no chassis or suspension changes were named. The 2027 450 XCF-W lists 107.5 kg without fuel, a WP XACT 48 mm fork (300 mm), a WP XPLOR PDS shock (310 mm), 963 mm seat height and an 8.5 L tank.

source.name: Powersports Business: KTM refreshes enduro range for 2027 model year

records.notes: Weights/specs from KTM USA spec page. A 300 XC-W Hard Enduro is also listed for 2027 in the US. European coverage (Visordown, 2026-06) calls the EXC range changes subtle and mainly cosmetic.

records.statement: The 2027 Husqvarna FC 250, FC 350 and FC 450 return to the US after a missed 2026 year with white powder-coated chromoly frames, new Swedish-inspired graphics and engine updates for rideability and the latest sound rules; the platform is otherwise unchanged. US prices are $10,799, $11,199 and $11,749, with claimed weights of 224.2, 225.9 and 227.7 lb without fuel.

source.name: Cycle News: 2027 Husqvarna FC Motocrossers Specs and Prices

records.notes: Versus KTM SX-F: Husqvarna uses its own polyamide subframe/bodywork, ProTaper bars and a different silencer; quickshifter, traction control and launch control are standard on the 4-strokes. Cycle News lists FC 450 compression as 13.6:1 versus KTM's 13.1:1 (see conflicts).

records.statement: Husqvarna's 2027 cross-country range is the TX 300, FX 350 and the returning FX 450 (absent for 2026), all with new white powder-coated frames; the FX models keep quickshifter, traction control, launch control and two maps, and the TX 300 keeps throttle-body injection.

source.name: Enduro21: Quick Look 2027 Husqvarna cross-country range - FX 450 returns

records.notes: No mechanical changes named beyond frame finish. See ko4-013 for the 2026 FX 450 gap.

records.statement: Husqvarna's 2027 enduro range is a light-touch update with no announced engine, chassis or suspension changes: new yellow fork guards and shroud graphics, plus a new 12-month warranty programme. Australian coverage adds white powder-coated frames.

source.name: Enduro21: First look 2027 Husqvarna enduro range

records.notes: European/Australian coverage; TE 150 is not in the European list but is listed as a 2027 US model (Motorcycle.com spec page). Transmoto (2026-07) reports white frames for the enduro range too.

records.statement: GasGas USA lists 2027 MC 450F, MC 250F, MC 125, MC 85 (17/14 and 19/16), MC 65, MC 50, EX 300 and EC 300 models, with no 'new for 2027' text on its motocross page. Dealers describe the 2027 changes as new graphics, with updated bodywork and seat covers on the MC 250F.

source.name: GASGAS USA: Motocross models page

records.notes: UK dealer (Craigs, 2026-09) mentions unspecified 'mechanical refinements'. No 2027 MC 350F or EX 350F/450F seen on the US motocross page at fetch time.

records.statement: The 2027 GasGas MC 250F keeps a WP XACT 48 mm air fork and an unchanged shock, but unlike the KTM its traction control, quickshifter, launch control and two maps only work with the optional map-select switch; it uses Maxxis MaxxCross MX-ST tyres and Braktec brakes instead of Dunlop MX34 and Brembo. US price is $9,899 and claimed weight 102 kg without fuel; the airbox and exhaust were last updated for 2026 sound rules.

source.name: GASGAS USA: MC 250F 2027 model page

records.notes: Manufacturer model page.

records.statement: The 2027 GasGas MC 450F carries over with new graphics; a spec listing gives $10,849 MSRP, 13.1:1 compression and 228.4 lb dry.

source.name: Motorcycle.com: 2027 GASGAS MC 450F specs

records.notes: Spec-database figures; the same listing shows a 300 mm fork with preload/rebound adjustment only, which looks like a data error for a WP XACT air fork. No 2027 change list found.

records.statement: GasGas's 2027 EX 300 page lists a WP XACT closed-cartridge spring fork with internals revised against oil foaming, an unchanged shock, a frame 300 g lighter (slimmer upper shock mount, thinner front walls, lighter engine mounts), 39 mm Keihin throttle-body injection with electronic exhaust control, and the map switch as an option. Price is $11,099 and claimed weight 102.3 kg without fuel.

source.name: GASGAS USA: EX 300 2027 model page

records.notes: The page says EEC was 'introduced last year', so much of this copy describes 2025-2026 updates carried into 2027 rather than 2027-new changes.

records.statement: The 2027 GasGas EC 300 (and race-focused EC 300 GP) are listed in the 2027 enduro range with no specific changes published.

source.name: PERRY: 2027 GASGAS Motocross, Enduro & Cross Country range has arrived

records.notes: Dealer announcement; no change list found.

conflicts.note: 4.8 may be the tester's chosen rate, not stock; the 2026 X is said to carry RC settings.
Could be counting method or a running change.
Testers consistently run less sag than the handbook.
95 mm x 63.4 mm matches 449.9 cc; 94 mm is likely a typo.
Same engine family; 13.6 may be a press-sheet error or a different measuring basis. Verify with Husqvarna spec sheet.
